biological_interpretation: Resting neuronal MAPK output is branch-specific, with SHOC2 feeding a BRAF/MEK1-like Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 state and ERK2 transcript knockdown buffered or bypassed at the mRNA endpoint. / A directional RAF-MEK transcriptional readout is strongest at MEK1/BRAF/NF1 in thalamic glutamatergic neurons and is not a generic RAS-family or MEK-paralog null. / LZTR1 may act in the same thalamic RAS/MAPK polarity space as NF1 and RAF/MEK nodes, but the observed Lztr1 response remains weak. / NF1 loss derepresses a subtype-biased Ras/MAPK feedback state in mature neurons, with CIC overlapping only partially rather than serving as a full NF1 proxy. / The atlas recovers the expected polarity of Ras/MAPK regulation at the transcriptome level in selected neuronal classes, while wild-type Hras loss is not a proxy for activated-HRAS or NF1-loss states.
caveats: Raf1 mRNA engagement in 151 and 066 was weak, and Araf had no perturbation rows.
The contrast is based on one cell type and on RNA signatures rather than direct RAF isoform activity measurements.
Mapk1 had fewer perturbed cells than several comparators and only nominal target-transcript evidence in this cell type.
Rasa2 target engagement was weak; the comparison is between aggregate perturbation signatures rather than matched edits in identical cells.
Braf transcript depletion itself was not FDR-significant; the 066 response is one gene in 49 perturbed cells.
The Lztr1 genes used for the correlation were nominal only; full-transcriptome correlations were small.
Dusp4, Dusp6 and Spry4 support is nominal rather than FDR-level; Vgf is an activity/neurotrophin gene and is not specific to NF1.
MAPK perturbations target upstream kinases/regulators and need not equal acute ERK-mediated CIC phosphorylation; the comparison is transcriptome-wide and same-cell-type but not time-resolved.
The comparison was restricted to genes with Nf1 nominal p<0.001; correlations are transcriptomic and do not measure ERK phosphorylation.
Counts of significant genes do not align perturbations by biochemical direction; the compared targets differ in editing efficiency, pathway position and loss-of-function consequence.
Map2k1 self-knockdown was nominal with FDR=1.0, and the significant genes were not connected to MAPK by the sources used here.

Exact log2 fold changes, scores, p-values, and FDRs in exact_de_rows were re-read from the Wilcoxon Parquet; the graph and cluster summaries were used only to nominate the target/readout combinations.
exact_observed_result: The 151 TH Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 MAPK module was repressed by Braf and Map2k1 loss and induced by Nf1 loss; Shoc2 was preferentially Braf/Map2k1-like, whereas Raf1, Map2k2, Mapk1, Ptpn1, and Rasa2 failed to reproduce the module. / In 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c Glut, Map2k1 and Braf loss repressed a focused Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a/Etv5 program, Nf1 loss moved the axis oppositely, and Map2k2 did not reproduce the MEK1-sensitive module. / In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, a nominal Lztr1 module was concordant with Nf1 loss and opposed to Braf, Kras, Map2k1, and Shoc2 loss, giving weak Lztr1 downstream DE a directionally interpretable RAS/MAPK readout. / Nf1 perturbation induced Egr1, Etv4, Etv5, Dusp4, Dusp6, Spry4, Ptpn5, Unc13a, Scg2, Tnfrsf12a, and Vgf most strongly in thalamic and midbrain subclasses; Cic loss shared only a subset of these MAPK-responsive genes in the same thalamic hotspot. / Braf, Map2k1, and Mapk1 loss-of-function signatures opposed Nf1 on Nf1-responsive genes in 151 TH, 155 MB, and 191 MB P MY GABA, consistent with NF1 loss derepressing Ras while RAF/MEK/ERK loss reduces pathway flux. Parquet-verified leading rows: Cic->Lrrc7 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.39, FDR 1.24e-16; Nf1->Vgf in 155 MB Glut log2FC 2.19, FDR 1.75e-16; Nf1->Vgf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC 0.848, FDR 1.36e-11; Cic->Spock3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.395, FDR 6.01e-10; Cic->Atp2a2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.274, FDR 1.35e-09; Nf1->Vgf in 191 MB P MY GABA log2FC 1.87, FDR 1.78e-09.

prior_expectation.summary: References were retained only when they were linked to one of the resolved source findings.

finding_summaries.summary: Raf1 did not reproduce the Braf Vgf/Ptpn5 phenotype in the responsive thalamic/hypothalamic classes, while Araf was not assayed.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: This argues that the observed output may be Braf-biased rather than interchangeable across RAF paralogs, a useful refinement when reasoning about RAF dimer and isoform biology in neurons.

finding_summaries.summary: The thalamic Shoc2 RNA output is Braf/Map2k1-weighted and is not reproduced by Raf1 or Map2k2.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: SHOC2 is capable of controlling RAF-family phosphoserines, but these data show that individual RAF and MEK paralogs are not interchangeable at the level of steady-state neuronal RNA output.

finding_summaries.summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained a Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 Ras-MAPK output for Braf, Map2k1, Ntrk2, and Nf1 perturbations that direct Mapk1 perturbation failed to reproduce.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: This preserves the strongest related-target divergence: the pathway can be read out in this cell class, but the ERK2 node is buffered or compensated relative to upstream activators and the NF1 Ras brake.

finding_summaries.summary: Rasa2 and Nf1 diverged sharply despite both belonging to the RasGAP regulatory layer.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: The contrast preserves the non-interchangeability of RasGAP nodes: Nf1 was sufficient to drive Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 or Vgf/Egr1 programs, whereas Rasa2 was not.

finding_summaries.direction: downstream genes decreased by Braf perturbation
finding_summaries.summary: Braf perturbation yielded transcriptome-wide significant output in only two cell classes, with a four-gene Vgf/Ptpn5/Atp2a2/Unc13a module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a Vgf-only signal in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: The dataset localizes a canonical BRAF-MAPK transcriptional response to a narrow neuronal context instead of supporting uniform Braf dependence across assayed brain populations.

finding_summaries.direction: Lztr1 and Nf1 loss up; Braf, Map2k1, Kras, and Shoc2 loss down for the restricted module
finding_summaries.summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the nominal Lztr1 module is concordant with Nf1 loss and opposed to Braf, Kras, Map2k1, and Shoc2 loss, matching de-repression of RAS/MAPK signaling.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: This converts otherwise weak Lztr1 downstream DE into a directionally interpretable pathway readout in one neuronal class.

finding_summaries.summary: Nf1 perturbation repeatedly induced a Vgf-centered neurotrophin/activity output with nominal-to-FDR support for Ras/MAPK feedback genes.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: The dominant response is not simply detectible Nf1 mRNA loss; it is a coherent downstream transcriptional state consistent with derepression of Ras/RAF/MEK/ERK signaling in selected neurons.

finding_summaries.summary: Cic loss only partially phenocopies Ras/MAPK perturbations in the TH hotspot.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: CIC is regulated downstream of RTK/Ras/ERK signaling, but the Cic signature is not reducible to a generic MAPK-activity signature: Nf1, Braf, Map2k1, and Map2k2 perturbations show near-zero global score correlations with Cic even though shared MAPK-responsive genes such as Ptpn5, Dusp4, and Etv5 move in the expected subset of the signature.

finding_summaries.summary: Braf, Map2k1 and Mapk1 loss-of-function signatures were opposite to Nf1 on the Nf1-responsive gene subset.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: This inverse relationship is the expected sign if Nf1 loss derepresses an upstream Ras signal while RAF/MEK/ERK perturbations reduce downstream pathway flux.

finding_summaries.summary: Hras did not phenocopy downstream RAS/MAPK or mTOR-axis perturbations that were significant in the same neuronal classes.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: RASopathy and Ras-effector genes cannot be collapsed to one expected transcriptomic direction in this screen: Nf1, Braf/Map2k/Mapk and Tsc/Pten perturbations generated corrected signatures in thalamic or midbrain classes where Hras remained silent.

finding_summaries.summary: The 191 MB P MY GABA response is statistically supported but does not resemble the TH Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 MAPK module.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: Not every FDR-positive Map2k1 effect should be annotated as a canonical ERK transcriptional program; this subclass produced Las1l and Uso1 changes without FDR-supported Vgf, Ptpn5, Unc13a, or Etv5.

resolved_evidence.statistics: 052 Pvalb Gaba: 77 cells, Vgf logFC 1.113, FDR 0.00239. 054 CNU-MGE GABA: 59 cells, Vgf logFC 1.462, FDR 3.80e-5 and Unc13a logFC 0.445, FDR 0.0205. 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA: 71 cells, Vgf logFC 1.648, FDR 5.47e-8; Etv5 logFC 1.139, p=2.36e-5, FDR 0.135; Egr1 logFC 0.908, p=2.03e-4, FDR 0.696.

resolved_evidence.description: Several canonical Ras/MAPK transcriptional feedback markers were repeatedly induced, mostly below FDR thresholds.
resolved_evidence.statistics: At nominal p<0.05 and positive logFC, Etv5 recurred in 9 Nf1 cell types, Etv4 in 5, Dusp4 in 7, Dusp6 in 5, and Spry4 in 4. Etv5 reached FDR 0.0127 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; Etv4 reached FDR 0.0424 in 191 MB P MY GABA.

resolved_evidence.description: Related Ras/MAPK perturbations showed pathway activity but were nearly uncorrelated with Cic at the whole-signature level.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Score correlations with the Cic signature were Nf1 r=0.002, Braf r=0.004, Map2k1 r=0.071, and Map2k2 r=0.097 over 17,259 genes. In the same cell type, Nf1 perturbation produced 12 FDR hits including Vgf +0.848 FDR 1.36e-11, Ptpn5 +0.550 FDR 1.64e-8, and Etv5 +0.541 FDR 0.0127; Braf and Map2k1 perturbations downregulated the same axis, including Braf Vgf -0.795 FDR 1.39e-4 and Map2k1 Vgf -0.785 FDR 7.85e-8.

resolved_evidence.description: Canonical CIC/MAPK transcriptional outputs are present but are not the dominant Cic response in the thalamic hotspot.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Within the Cic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature, Dusp4 was upregulated (logFC +0.785, FDR 0.0296) and Ptpn5 was upregulated (logFC +0.313, FDR 7.53e-4). Etv5 was nominally up (logFC +0.312, p=0.00402, FDR 0.0941), Spry4 was nominally up (logFC +0.527, p=0.00201, FDR 0.0567), and Etv1 and Etv4 were not nominally significant in this cell type (p=0.738 and p=0.407).

resolved_evidence.description: Loss-of-function of downstream RAF/MEK/ERK genes tended to shift Nf1-responsive genes in the opposite direction.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Pearson correlations were computed on genes with Nf1 nominal p<0.001 in the same cell type. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, n=111: Braf r=-0.391, Map2k1 r=-0.437, Mapk1 r=-0.223. In 155 MB Glut, n=107: Braf r=-0.578, Map2k1 r=-0.346, Mapk1 r=-0.576. In 191 MB P MY GABA, n=91: Braf r=-0.442, Map2k1 r=-0.356, Mapk1 r=-0.264.

resolved_evidence.description: A thalamic glutamatergic class with adequate Hras coverage showed strong responses to several pathway-neighbor perturbations but not to Hras.
resolved_evidence.statistics: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Hras n=162 cells and 0 FDR<0.05 genes, whereas Braf n=137 had 4, Map2k1 n=177 had 4, Nf1 n=152 had 12, Lztr1 n=232 had 1, Tsc1 n=164 had 321, and Tsc2 n=177 had 86 FDR<0.05 genes.

resolved_evidence.description: A midbrain glutamatergic class separated silent Hras perturbation from significant MAPK and mTOR-axis perturbation signatures.
resolved_evidence.statistics: In 155 MB Glut, Hras n=139 cells and 0 FDR<0.05 genes, whereas Map2k1 n=142 had 1, Mapk1 n=100 had 1, Nf1 n=113 had 2, Pten n=130 had 11, Tsc1 n=166 had 478, and Tsc2 n=195 had 202 FDR<0.05 genes.

resolved_evidence.description: The mTOR-inhibitory TSC complex generated corrected perturbation programs in several classes where Hras remained buffered.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Tsc1/Tsc2 FDR<0.05 counts in four Hras nominal-engagement contexts were 89/53 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 94/2 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 321/86 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 478/202 in 155 MB Glut; Hras had 0 in each.

resolved_evidence.description: Restricted transcriptome-wide score correlations did not reveal a strong signed Hras phenocopy among related perturbations.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Wilcoxon-score correlations to Hras across matched genes were weak for pathway neighbors: maximum absolute r across matched cell types was 0.161 for Kras, 0.224 for Braf, 0.152 for Map2k1, 0.136 for Mapk1, 0.210 for Nf1, 0.084 for Tsc1, and 0.262 for Tsc2.

resolved_evidence.description: A second FDR-supported Map2k1 signature outside the TH module, with measured genes not obviously belonging to the canonical Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 response.
resolved_evidence.statistics: 96 perturbed cells versus 10309 controls; Las1l logFC -0.681, p=2.91e-6, FDR=0.0389; Uso1 logFC +0.647, p=4.55e-6, FDR=0.0389; Map2k1 self logFC -0.872, p=0.00130, FDR=1.0.

resolved_evidence.description: Most Map2k1 perturbation contexts lacked an FDR-supported downstream transcriptome.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Excluding the target transcript, 20/22 Map2k1 subclasses had zero genes at FDR<0.05; only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had four non-target FDR hits and 191 MB P MY GABA had two.

title: Braf/Map2k1/Shoc2, but not Raf1 or Mapk1, gate the TH Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 MAPK output
